THE BODY AND EMOTIONS

</p>

</p>

<h2>A body-oriented therapeutic approach</h2>

<p>Bioenergetic psychotherapy builds on the work of Alexander Lowen and the idea that body and mind are deeply interconnected aspects of our experience. Emotions are expressed not only through thoughts and words, but also through the way we breathe, move, hold ourselves, and sense our bodies.</p>

<p>The bioenergetic approach combines therapeutic dialogue with attention to bodily sensations, breathing, movement, and muscular tension to foster greater self-awareness and insight into ways of relating to others. <strong>The body thus becomes a pathway to understanding emotional experience</strong>, in a process that respects each person's pace, needs, and personal history.</p>
:::

</section>

<p class="eyebrow">

THE MIND AND ITS PROCESSES

</p>

<h2>Understanding cognitive functioning across the lifespan</h2>

<p>Neuropsychology studies the relationships between brain functioning, cognitive processes, and behaviour. Attention, memory, language, learning, and executive functions shape how each of us understands the world, handles everyday experiences, and relates to others.</p>

<p>Across the lifespan, these abilities develop, change, and interact continuously with emotional, psychological, and environmental factors. Neuropsychological assessment therefore goes beyond measuring individual test scores: it aims to build an overall profile of cognitive functioning, identifying strengths, potential vulnerabilities, and individual characteristics.</p>

<p><strong> Understanding how the mind works means looking beyond symptoms and considering the whole person. </strong> Cognitive assessment can therefore help guide clinical care, clarify difficulties, and identify personalised support strategies.</p>
